record.context_brief: star-shaped cmc surfaces with circular boundary
record.original_question: Is every compact star-shaped constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 with circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3 (5*). Is a compact star-shaped cmc surface of R3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of whether every compact cmc surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a circle must be a planar disk or a spherical cap is a well-known long-standing open question (commonly attributed to a conjecture going back to work of Nitsche/Alexandrov-type rigidity). Partial results are known under additional hypotheses (e.g. disk topology with stability, embeddedness with small area, or contact-angle conditions), but a full resolution—even under the star-shaped assumption—does not appear in the literature surveyed. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Constant Mean Curvature Disks with Circular Boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys partial results: e.g. a cmc disk with area at most that of the spherical cap is a spherical cap; uniqueness under various extra hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial uniqueness results are known for cmc surfaces with circular boundary.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature surfaces with circular boundary in R^3
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the open question of classifying cmc surfaces in R^3 spanning a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The full classification of cmc surfaces spanning a circle is still an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (Lopez)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including whether cmc surfaces with circular boundary must be umbilical under additional hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in general; only special cases are settled.
